messages:
Lina: Quick question — what's the minimal console/iam scope we can give an SRE to debug pod logs for a single k8s namespace without exposing raw PII fields? Need this for a short 1-2h troubleshooting window.

samuel: Are you talking about Cloud Logging (Logs Explorer) entries or some 3rd-party log agg?

Lina: Cloud Logging (GCP). Logs contain user_email and some customer identifiers we need redacted. We just want them to see non-PII fields and timestamps for debugging. Ideally namespace-limited.

mike_g: Two quick calls here: 1) IAM alone can't redact fields. It limits access to logs but if they have access to the logEntry they can see the payload. 2) Pattern that works: create a redacted view of the logs (sink -> transform -> write to a separate destination) and give the SRE access to that destination, or grant ephemeral access to the real logs only when needed.

mike_g: Minimal permissions if you go ephemeral: a short-lived SA with a custom role that includes: `logging.logEntries.list` and `logging.logEntries.get` scoped to the project(s) containing the cluster. Avoid broad viewer perms. Also restrict via org/project-level IAM bindings + resource-scoped policies where possible.

Lina: Any concrete steps/examples?

mike_g: Example flow we use:
1) Create a Logs Router sink that sends matching namespace logs to a Pub/Sub topic.
2) A small Cloud Function subscribes, redacts sensitive fields, writes to a separate Logging bucket / BigQuery dataset.
3) Grant SRE role access only to the redacted destination.

mike_g: Snippet — create a sink (filters by namespace):
```
gcloud logging sinks create redacted-sink pubsub.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT/topics/REDACTED-LOGS \
  --log-filter='resource.type="k8s_container" AND labels.k8s-pod/namespace="my-namespace"'
```
Then hook a function to redact and write to a new dataset/bucket.

samuel: If you can't build the redaction pipeline right away, use JIT ephemeral access: create a short-lived service account key (or use Workload Identity Federation / short-lived tokens) and bind a custom role for 1-2 hours. Make sure the grant is logged and approved in the ticket.

security-bot: Policy note: any temporary elevation must be ticketed and include justification + approver. Also ensure log access is audited — maintain audit logs for who viewed raw logs.

Lina: For the custom role, any recommended least-perm definition I can hand to infra folks?

mike_g: Keep it tight. Example permissions list (strings you can put into the custom role):
- `logging.logEntries.list`
- `logging.logEntries.get` (optional, only if they need full payload)
- `resourcemanager.projects.get` (maybe, to list project meta) — avoid if not needed

mike_g: If you truly want to prevent viewing PII, don't grant `logging.logEntries.get` on the raw logs. Instead give access only to the redacted destination. If you must grant `list` to find entries, pair it with an approval workflow and short TTL.

Lina: Cool. I'll open a ticket to create the redacted sink and a 2hr ephemeral SA bound to the redacted destination. For now we'll request a 1-hour JIT on the real logs with approver @samuel.

samuel: fine with that — confirm the ticket references this thread and include the exact filter + TTL.

mike_g: Also add a note to the ticket to rotate/delete any created keys after use.

security-bot: Reminder: if PII is present, check our data retention and redaction policy before exporting to BigQuery. Use encryption and limit dataset IAM.

Lina: Thanks all — I'll post the ticket link here once created. :thumbsup:
